thread.title: Big Media Deals That Could Happen in 2019---and Some That Won't

title: Big Media Deals That Could Happen in 2019---and Some That Won't
text:
Big Media Deals That Could Happen in 2019—and Some That Won’t By Jan. 7, 2019 2:51 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Tomohiro Ohsumi/Getty Images Text size
CBS (CBS) will buy Viacom (VIA) in 2019—and that's just one of the deals you should expect this year, according to a media analyst.
BTIG’s Rich Greenfield on Monday published a post sharing predictions for media and technology companies in the year ahead. Many of them covered possible deals, with CBS buying Viacom—something he’s been predicting for years—among them. So, what’s changed?
That would be the removal of former CBS CEO Les Moonves , according to Greenfield.
“Moonves put his own personal self-interest above shareholders,” Greenfield wrote. “Rather than name a new CEO, we believe CBS’ board of directors should reopen merger discussions with Viacom immediately. A transaction could be effected relatively quickly with the support of both Viacom and CBS’ Boards.”
His other deal-related predictions: Newsletter Sign-up
• A “FAANG” company— Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon.com (AMZN) or Netflix (NFLX)—buys a videogame studio, potentially a major one.
“While Amazon and Google are the ones to watch, we would not sleep on Facebook and Apple, the former who has been largely unsuccessful in its games ambitions (especially video) since it essentially helped launch Zynga (ZNGA), and the latter which has a need to diversify its revenue streams,” wrote Greenfield.
He sees privately owned Bethesda as the “most obvious” target, but says any of the top publishers—including Electronic Arts (EA) , Activision Blizzard (ATVI), and Take-Two Interactive (TTWO)—could be candidates.
• Walmart (WMT) will buy Roku (ROKU) . The latter company is frequently the subject of acquisition speculation , and the massive retailer is sometimes discussed as a buyer as it looks to take on Netflix and others.
“If the goal is to increase time spent with Walmart to drive retail spending (as Prime Video does for Amazon), we believe acquiring Roku could be Walmart’s most compelling entry point into streaming video,” Greenfield wrote.
Greenfield’s observation may have contributed to a lift in Roku shares Monday on the back of the release of some upbeat operational numbers .
• Fox—the part that wasn’t sold to Walt Disney (DIS)—will reacquire most of the regional sports networks, YES Network aside, that Disney had to divest to complete the deal. (Nicholas Jasinski covered this subject for Barron’s late last year.)
“Fox knows and loves the regional sports networks, with the acquisition of these assets at a fraction of the price that Fox sold them to Disney, adding to New Fox’s sports prowess,” wrote Greenfield.”
• Finally, some deals Greenfield doesn’t think will happen: NBCUniversal, majority-owned by Comcast (CMCSA), won’t bail out of consortium-owned Hulu, and three companies—Zynga, Snap (SNAP) and AMC Networks (AMCX)—won’t sell.
